f2l.title: F2L Guide
f2l.introBody: F2L replaces the beginner's step of solving middle-layer edges one at a time with something much faster: pairing up a corner with its matching edge and placing them together in one motion. Done well, this step is usually the biggest chunk of a CFOP solve — which is also why it's the biggest place to gain speed.
f2l.coreIdeaBody: After the cross, four corner-edge pairs need to go into the last four slots. Instead of solving them as separate pieces, find a corner and edge that share two colors, combine them into a pair using the top layer as free space, and insert the pair into its slot in one motion. Most cases don't need a memorized algorithm at all — they fall out of understanding a small set of recurring moves (this is what J Perm and most speedcubers mean by "intuitive F2L").
f2l.speedTip1Body: Spend time understanding why a pair comes together and slots in the way it does before reaching for an algorithm sheet. Algorithms without understanding fall apart the moment a case looks slightly different from the picture.
f2l.speedTip2Body: Every rotation costs recognition time. Learn to track pieces relative to the R and F faces without turning your whole grip.
f2l.speedTip3Body: While finishing the cross, look for your first pair. While inserting one pair, already track the next. This is the single biggest lever for real solving speed, bigger than any algorithm swap.
f2l.speedTip4Body: Once your intuitive solutions are solid (a common benchmark is sub-15-second solves), F2L algorithm sheets become useful — for optimizing awkward cases and back-slot insertions, not for learning the step from scratch.
f2l.speedTip5Body: Learn to tell whether the cross-color sticker on a piece is showing on top or on the side — it changes which setup move combines the pair without flipping the edge twice.
